t: Aim and plan of the session
n: In this session we will become familiar with the analysis of phenylalkylamines and precursors. Phenylalkylamines form the basis of most synthetic narcotic drugs; this group is known as amphetamine derivatives. The aim is to learn to isolate and detect ephedrine and ephedrone in urine, to carry out preliminary analysis of amphetamines, and to detect precursors, that is acetic anhydride and KMnO4. The plan has three parts. First, ephedrine and ephedrone. Second, amphetamines: Marquis reagent and TLC. Third, precursors: acetic anhydride, potassium permanganate, toluene, acetone and acids.

Four outcomes are expected from the session. First, to isolate ephedrine and ephedrone from urine and detect them with the Dragendorff, Reinecke salt and copper-CS2 reactions. Second, to distinguish on TLC ephedrine, with an Rf value of 0.28, and ephedrone, with an Rf value of 0.71. Third, to evaluate the colour of amphetamines with Marquis reagent by Table 11 and to read the TLC result by Table 12. Fourth, to detect acetic anhydride and potassium permanganate by qualitative reactions.

Reagents and equipment. For isolation, a 10% potassium carbonate solution, pH=10, and chloroform are used; for ephedrone, acetic acid and KMnO4, with oxidation conditions of 50-60 °C. For the reactions, Dragendorff's reagent, a fresh 1% solution of Reinecke salt, a 5% solution of copper sulphate, ammonia and a CS2-benzene mixture 1:3 are needed. In TLC, chloroform and acetone in the ratio 48:2 are used, and the developing agent is a solution of ninhydrin in acetone. For precursors, iron (III) chloride, lanthanum nitrate, iodine, H2O2, sulphuric acid, KI and sodium thiosulphate, 0.1 N, are used.

Safety rules. The student brings rubber gloves, a wipe and a face mask to the laboratory work. The examination is carried out in rooms with ventilation and a fume cupboard; after the work the rooms are locked and sealed. Acetic anhydride is a highly corrosive substance; its vapours irritate the eyes, nose and throat. Objects from infectious persons, that is those with tuberculosis, hepatitis or AIDS, arrive in a special container and are marked in the documents.

Classification of phenylalkylamines. On the illegal market more than 20 substances of this group occur, and more than a hundred derivatives have been synthesised. The classification is conventional: natural and synthetic groups are distinguished, and the synthetic ones are divided into 3 classes. In the first class the hydrogen of the amino group is substituted, in the second the hydrogen of the alkyl group, in the third the hydrogen of the benzene ring. The first representatives were found in plants: edible khat, the herb ephedra and the peyote cactus.

t: Classification of phenylalkylamines: in more detail
n: Let us look at the classification of phenylalkylamines in more detail. They are conventionally divided into natural and synthetic groups; the synthetic ones are split into 3 classes. Derivatives with a substituted benzene ring hydrogen include the monomethoxy, that is PMA, the dimethoxy, that is DOM and DOB, and the methylenedioxy, that is MDA and MDMA. The trimethoxy derivatives include 3,4,5-trimethoxyamphetamine and mescaline. The natural group includes khat, ephedra and the peyote cactus.

There are three natural sources. The leaves of edible khat, that is Catha edulis, contain the alkaloids cathinone and cathine; the active components make up 0.5-2%. On drying, cathinone evaporates. The ephedra plant contains ephedrine and pseudoephedrine, of which only ephedrine is significant. The powder of the flowers of the peyote cactus, that is Lophophora williamsii, contains up to 8% mescaline. That is, each plant has its own active substance.

Properties and significance of ephedrine. The ephedra plant contains the alkaloids ephedrine and pseudoephedrine, but only ephedrine is significant. Ephedrine as the base dissolves well in ethyl alcohol, ether and chloroform, and its hydrochloride salt in water and alcohol. Its action is similar to adrenaline: it raises blood pressure, constricts vessels and stimulates the central nervous system. Of the dose taken, 80% is excreted unchanged in the urine within a day.

Let us distinguish ephedrine and ephedrone. Ephedrone is an oxidation product of ephedrine; both are excreted in the urine. With Reinecke salt, ephedrine gives four-sided reddish-pink crystals, while ephedrone gives thin crystals with straight edges. On TLC, in the chloroform and acetone 48:2 system, ephedrine has Rf=0.28 and ephedrone Rf=0.71. In the ultraviolet spectrum, ephedrine gives maxima at 251, 257, 263 nm, and ephedrone in HCl a maximum at 251 nm.

How ephedrone is obtained from ephedrine. Ephedrone causes strong euphoria; for analysis the urine of toxicomaniacs and the liquids they have consumed are taken. Drug addicts obtain ephedrone from ephedrine by oxidising it with potassium permanganate and acetic acid at 50-60 °C. Signs: tachycardia, mydriasis, dry skin, raised blood pressure, arrhythmia; it quickly causes dependence.

Scheme of the preparation of ephedrone. The starting substance is ephedrine, and the reagents are potassium permanganate and acetic acid. Oxidation proceeds at 50-60 °C, and ephedrone is formed as a result. Ephedrone causes strong euphoria; tachycardia, mydriasis, raised blood pressure and arrhythmia are observed. Most important, it quickly causes dependence.

t: Isolating ephedrine and ephedrone from urine
n: Isolating ephedrine and ephedrone from urine. Ephedrine and ephedrone are excreted in the urine, so the main object is urine. The urine is made alkaline, to pH=10, with a 10% solution of potassium carbonate. It is then extracted with chloroform, and the resulting extract is sent for analysis.

With Dragendorff's reagent both ephedrine and ephedrone form dark red needle-shaped crystals, so it does not distinguish between them. To distinguish them, Reinecke salt is used: its fresh 1% solution is applied, and after 5-10 minutes it is examined under the microscope. Ephedrine gives four-sided reddish-pink crystals; ephedrone gives thin crystals with straight edges.

t: Reaction with copper salt and CS2
n: Reaction with copper salt and CS2. 1-2 drops of the solution are acidified with acetic acid, then 5% copper sulphate and ammonia are added. Then 2 drops of a CS2 and benzene mixture, in the ratio 1:3, are added and shaken. With ephedrine, the benzene layer becomes yellow or brown. With ephedrone, a dithiocarbamic acid derivative forms and the benzene layer turns yellow-brown.

t: Copper salt and CS2 reaction: scheme
n: Scheme of the copper-CS2 reaction. 1-2 drops of the solution are acidified with acetic acid, and 5% copper sulphate and ammonia are added. Then 2 drops of a CS2 and benzene mixture, in the ratio 1:3, are added and shaken. With ephedrine, the benzene layer becomes yellow or brown. With ephedrone, a dithiocarbamic acid derivative forms and the benzene layer turns yellow-brown.

We distinguish ephedrine and ephedrone on TLC. System: chloroform and acetone in the ratio 48:2. The spots are detected by spraying with a solution of ninhydrin in acetone. For ephedrine Rf=0.28, for ephedrone Rf=0.71. That is, ephedrone sits higher on the plate.

Let us sum up the Rf values and systems for TLC. For ephedrine and ephedrone, the chloroform and acetone system, 48:2, and a solution of ninhydrin in acetone are used; Rf=0.28 and 0.71. Another system is chloroform and acetone, 9:1: a mixture of ephedrine and ephedrone gives an ink-coloured spot on a pink background. Phenylalkylamines in the general system, in the ratio 20:3:1:20, give Rf=0.36.

UV spectrum and quantitative analysis. The acidic solution of ephedrine absorbs light with maxima at 251, 257 and 263 nm. A solution of ephedrone in 0.1 M HCl absorbs with a maximum at 251 nm, and in 0.1 M alkali at 247 nm. The quantity of ephedrine is determined by UV spectrophotometry using a graph of absorbance against concentration. The quantity of ephedrone is determined on the photoelectrocolorimeter by the absorbance of the copper-CS2 complex, or by the absorbance of the solution in HCl.

General isolation of phenylalkylamines. They are isolated from the biological object by the acidified water or alcohol method. The aqueous extract is brought to pH 9-12 and extracted three times with chloroform; the chloroform layer is filtered through anhydrous Na2SO4. Blood, 10 ml, or urine, 50 ml, is brought to pH 10-11 with 25% ammonia and extracted 3 times with a mixture of chloroform and n-butanol, in the ratio 9:1. After evaporation 0.5-1 ml remains, and it is given for chemical and physicochemical analysis.

Mescaline in numbers. Mescaline was first isolated from the peyote cactus in 1896. At a dose of 200-500 mg it has a hallucinogenic effect. The effect begins in 30-60 minutes and lasts 4-6 hours; it is 4000 times weaker than LSD. At a dose of 5-10 mg/kg tremor and hallucinations are seen; at 20 mg/kg paralysis of the respiratory centre and death may occur.

Amphetamine and methamphetamine. Amphetamine is a colourless, volatile, oily liquid with a "fishy" odour; boiling point 200-203 °C. Its dextrorotatory isomer acts on the central nervous system 3-4 times more strongly and causes strong psychological dependence. Methamphetamine is d-N-methylamphetamine, a white powder with a bitter taste and no odour. It was synthesised in 1919 and is distributed under the name "Ice".

Let us compare amphetamine and methamphetamine. Amphetamine is an oily liquid with a fishy odour, boiling point 200-203 °C; the dextrorotatory isomer is 3-4 times stronger. Methamphetamine is a white powder without odour, synthesised in 1919; it is distributed under the name "Ice" or "Glass" and is synthesised from ephedrine. In appearance, odour and history they differ considerably.

MDA and MDMA. MDA was synthesised in 1910. At a dose below 80 mg it stimulates, at 150 mg it causes hallucinations, and above 500 mg it leads to death. An MDA tablet contains 200-230 mg of methylenedioxyamphetamine. MDMA was synthesised in 1914; its single dose is 100 mg, the effect begins in 30-60 minutes and lasts 4-6 hours.

Let us compare the methylenedioxy derivatives. MDA was synthesised in 1910, MDMA in 1914, MDEA in 1980. MDA at a dose below 80 mg stimulates, at 150 mg it causes hallucinations, and above 500 mg it leads to death. The single dose of MDMA is 100 mg; the effect begins in 30-60 minutes and lasts 4-6 hours. MDEA, however, causes strong hallucinations.

About DOM, or STP. It was synthesised in 1963 by A. Shulgin and appeared in the USA in 1967. It is 80-100 times stronger than mescaline, and 50-60 times weaker than LSD. The name STP is an abbreviation of the words Serenity, that is carefreeness, Tranquility, that is calmness, and Peace.

Preliminary analysis: tablet and powder. In "ecstasy" tablets, caffeine, aspirin, paracetamol, ephedrine, quinine, lidocaine and others occur. For analysis, 5-10 mg of the tablet is ground in a mortar, transferred to a porcelain dish and 2-3 drops of Marquis reagent are added. The formation of a colour with Marquis reagent is regarded as a preliminary sign. The result is then confirmed by TLC.

Table 11: colours with Marquis reagent. MDA, MDMA, MDEA, MBDB and BDB give a bluish-black, that is green-black, colour. DOM, or STP, gives a yellow colour; PMA light grey, TMA orange, DOB emerald green. Mescaline gives orange, and methamphetamine a brown colour. Consequently, the colour gives a preliminary direction, but does not distinguish the methylenedioxy derivatives from one another.

Table 12: TLC results. System: chloroform, acetone, ethanol and 25% ammonia, in the ratio 20:3:1:20; Merck and Sorbfil plates are used. The colours with Marquis reagent and ninhydrin are evaluated together with Rf. MDA Rf 0.44, MDMA 0.12; their colour with Marquis reagent is the same, but they are distinguished with ninhydrin: yellow and violet. Methamphetamine Rf 0.25, mescaline Rf 0.36.

Let us distinguish phenylalkylamines by their UV spectra. Amphetamine, methamphetamine and ephedrine give maxima at 251, 257 and 263 nm in 0.1 M HCl. Ephedrone gives a maximum only at 251 nm. For MDA and MDMA the maxima are 235 and 286 nm; for N-ethyl-MDA and MBDB 234 and 286 nm.

The concept of precursors. Precursors are substances that are included in a list and are under control in Uzbekistan, and are used in preparing narcotic and psychotropic substances. Under the 1988 UN convention, 26 substances have been placed under international control; on 19 August 1999 the law on narcotic drugs was adopted. The 29 substances on the list are divided into two groups: those entering the synthesis and auxiliary ones, that is those playing the main role.

t: Table 18: precursor and the substance obtained
n: Table 18 shows the precursor and the substance obtained from it. Acetic anhydride is used in preparing methaqualone and heroin. Potassium permanganate is used in preparing methcathinone, and ephedrine is also a precursor for methcathinone. Pseudoephedrine is used in obtaining pervitin. Acetone, toluene and diethyl ether are used as solvents in preparing many narcotic drugs.

There are three main groups of precursors. Solvents: acetone, toluene, methyl ethyl ketone, that is 2-butanone, and diethyl ether. Reagents: acetic anhydride, potassium permanganate, sulphuric and hydrochloric acids, red phosphorus. Starting substances: ephedrine, pseudoephedrine, anthranilic acid, safrole, isosafrole and ergotamine.

Acetic anhydride. This is a mobile, colourless liquid with a characteristic strong suffocating odour; it dissolves well in benzene, chloroform and ethyl alcohol. The permissible level in air is 3 mg/m3. Under the action of water and air moisture it is hydrolysed to acetic acid. Therefore qualitative reactions are carried out for the acetic acid formed.

Reactions for detecting acetic anhydride. The neutralised and evaporated residue gives a red colour with iron (III) chloride, turning brown on heating; sensitivity 0.5 mg. When lanthanum nitrate, an alcoholic solution of iodine and ammonia are added, a dark blue colour or precipitate forms. On heating with ethyl alcohol and concentrated sulphuric acid, the characteristic odour of ethyl acetate is given off. The quantity is determined by the neutralisation method.

The iron (III) chloride reaction. Acetic anhydride is hydrolysed to acetic acid under the action of water and air moisture. If iron (III) chloride is added to the neutralised and evaporated residue, a red-coloured product forms. On heating, the red colour turns brown. The sensitivity of the reaction corresponds to 0.5 mg of acetic acid.

Potassium permanganate, KMnO4. These are violet crystals, a strong oxidising and disinfecting substance; it is used in obtaining narcotic drugs. Identity is checked as follows: when hydrogen peroxide acts in the presence of sulphuric acid, the solution is decolourised. The quantity is determined in an acidic medium by adding KI: the iodine released is titrated with 0.1 N sodium thiosulphate, with starch as indicator.

Toluene, acetone and acids. Toluene, on heating with concentrated sulphuric acid and ammonium nitrate, forms a nitro compound, and an odour of bitter almonds is given off; the quantity is determined by GLC and HPLC. For acetone, the iodoform formation reaction, the sodium nitroprusside reaction, red-violet, and the o-nitrobenzaldehyde reaction, blue indigo, are used; it is determined by GLC. Sulphuric acid gives a white precipitate with barium salts, and hydrochloric acid gives a white precipitate with silver nitrate; the quantity is determined by neutralisation.

Identity reactions of acetone. Acetone forms iodoform with an alkaline solution of iodine, but this reaction is not characteristic of acetone. With sodium nitroprusside in alkali it gives a red-violet colour. With furfural and HCl a red colour forms. With o-nitrobenzaldehyde a blue colour, that is indigo, forms; indigo dissolves well in chloroform.

Interpreting the result. Ephedrine and ephedrone are excreted in the urine, so the main material for analysis is urine. With Dragendorff's reagent both give the same crystals; they are distinguished by Reinecke salt and the TLC Rf values, 0.28 and 0.71. Precursors are substances on the list; their detection shows that the substance is a reagent used for the synthesis of a narcotic drug.

Review questions. First: how is ephedrone obtained, show the chemical equation, and how can ephedrine and ephedrone be distinguished? Second: how is qualitative analysis of ephedrine carried out; give the methods of analysis of ephedrone. Third: what substances are called precursors, and in obtaining which narcotic drugs is potassium permanganate used? Fourth: what chemical methods of analysing acetone do you know, and how will you analyse sulphuric and hydrochloric acids?

Let us summarise. Ephedrine and ephedrone are isolated from urine with K2CO3 at pH=10 and with chloroform; they are detected by the Dragendorff, Reinecke and copper-CS2 reactions and by TLC. Amphetamines are tested with Marquis reagent, Table 11, and TLC, Table 12, and confirmed by UV spectrum. Acetic anhydride is detected through acetic acid, and KMnO4 through oxidation-reduction reactions.
